IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p157/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p157/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p157/r4.claim: إذ may be extra in the cited clauses from 2:30 and 31:13, where the sense is simply “and He said.”
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p157/r4.anchor: و (إذ) قد تزاد، كقوله: وإذ قال ربك للملائكة [البقرة: 30] .

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p157/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p157/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p157/r5.claim: He also cites Ibn Mayyada's line beginning إذ لا يزال as poetic evidence for the extra use of إذ.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p157/r5.anchor: وقال ابن ميادة : إذ لا يزال قائل: أبن أبن

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p101/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p101/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p101/r1.claim: The polytheist degrades himself by worshipping beings lower than, or at best equal to, himself, and wrongs himself by exposing himself to ruin and eternal Hell.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p101/r1.anchor: الإنسان المشرك يحط من قدر نفسه لأن الآلهة التي يعبدها تكون أحط منه، وقصارى الأمر أن تكون مثله

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p101/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p101/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p101/r2.claim: Luqman invokes injustice because people naturally hate being wronged, even though they may accept committing injustice against themselves.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p101/r2.anchor: الإنسان بطبيعته يكره الظلم، قد يرتضيه لنفسه لكن لا يرضى أن يقع عليه ظلم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p101/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p101/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p101/r3.claim: Luqman explains the reason for his prohibition rather than merely issuing a command; parents should explain reasons so children understand and are persuaded.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p101/r3.anchor: لا بد من ذكر السبب حتى يفهم لماذا، لا بد أن يعرف حتى يقتنع

ITQAN:v1p89#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p89#2/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p89#2/r7.claim: The author replies that Ibn Abbas knew the wording was broader but identified the intended referent, as the Prophet interpreted ظلم as shirk while Companions grasped its general scope.
ITQAN:v1p89#2/r7.anchor: أجيب عن ذلك بأنه لا يخفى عليه أن اللفظ أعم من السبب لكنه بين أن المراد باللفظ خاص

BURSEVI:v7p58#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p58#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p58#2/r1.claim: The son is called An'am, by which Luqman is also known as Abu An'am.
BURSEVI:v7p58#2/r1.anchor: انعم فهو أبو أنعم أي : يكنى به

BURSEVI:v7p58#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p58#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p58#2/r2.claim: Luqman admonishes his son; admonition is a rebuke joined with warning, while al-Khalil defines it as a reminder of good that softens the heart.

BURSEVI:v7p58#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p58#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p58#2/r3.claim: The diminutive يا بني conveys tenderness and affection, fitting advice intended for the son's happiness if he follows it.
BURSEVI:v7p58#2/r3.anchor: وهو تصغير رحمة وعطوفة ولهذا أوصاه بما فيه سعادته

BURSEVI:v7p58#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p58#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p58#2/r4.claim: Shirk means treating something besides God as His partner in worship; it is immense injustice because it equates the source of every favor with one that gives no favor.
BURSEVI:v7p58#2/r4.anchor: لا تعدل بالله شيئا في العبادة

BURSEVI:v7p58#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p58#2/r5.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v7p58#2/r5.claim: Shirk is injustice against oneself, and its gravity lies in its never being forgiven.
BURSEVI:v7p58#2/r5.anchor: في "كشف الأسرار" (بيدادى است برخويشتن بزرك) وعظمه

BURSEVI:v7p58#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p58#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p58#2/r6.claim: Luqman's son and wife were initially unbelievers but became Muslim through his efforts; unlike Noah's son and wife, Lot's daughters accepted faith while his wife did not and was turned to stone in one report.
BURSEVI:v7p58#2/r6.anchor: وكان ابنه وامرأته كافرين فما زال بهما حتى أسلما

BURSEVI:v7p58#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p58#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p58#2/r7.claim: Some say Luqman began his advice with the warning to avoid shirk.
BURSEVI:v7p58#2/r7.anchor: وعظ لقمان ابنه في ابتداء وعظه

BURSEVI:v7p58#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p58#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p58#2/r8.claim: Inwardly, admonition turns the self from what is below God and gives God alone the soul's service, the heart's attention, and the spirit's vision; this is individuation within unity.
BURSEVI:v7p58#2/r8.anchor: والوعظ زجر النفس عن الاشتغال بما دون الله

SULAMI:v2p130#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p130#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p130#2/r1.claim: Luqman's first counsel against associating partners with God is to single out the Real with one's whole self, heart, and spirit, serving and seeing none but Him.
SULAMI:v2p130#2/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : وعظ لقمان ابنه ودله في ابتداء وعظه على مجانبة الشرك

SULAMI:v2p130#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p130#2/r2.speaker: محمد بن علي
SULAMI:v2p130#2/r2.claim: Admonition is calling people to the Real and His way.
SULAMI:v2p130#2/r2.anchor: وقال محمد بن علي : الوعظ هو الدعاء إلى الحق وطريقته

NAHHAS:v3p283/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p283/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p283/r7.claim: إذ is accusative with an understood command to remember; Abu Ishaq instead attaches it to the gift of wisdom, which al-Nahhas rejects because of the wāw and word order.
NAHHAS:v3p283/r7.anchor: إذ في موضع نصب والمعنى واذكر وحكى أبو إسحاق في كتابه في القرآن أن إذ في موضع نصب بآياتنا

NAHHAS:v3p283/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p283/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p283/r8.claim: يا بني has kasra on yāʾ to indicate omitted yāʾ; some give fatḥa because it is lighter.
NAHHAS:v3p283/r8.anchor: يا بني ) بكسر الياء لأنها دالة على الياء المحذوفة ومن فتحها فلخفة الفتحة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p148/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p148/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p148/r1.claim: Reports with weak chains commonly describe Luqman as Black and place his origin in Nubia or Abyssinia.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p148/r1.anchor: وأكثر الروايات في شأنه التي يعضد بعضها وإن كانت أسانيدها ضعيفة تقتضي أنه كان من السود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p148/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p148/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p148/r2.claim: Quranic Luqman is distinct from Luqman ibn Ad, the proverb and vulture figure; some authors confused him with Balaam son of Beor in Numbers 22–23, probably through a mistaken shared paternal name or supposed name translation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p148/r2.anchor: وليس هو لقمان به عاد الذي قال المثل المشهور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p148/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p148/r3.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p148/r3.claim: Most early authorities regard Luqman as a wise, pious man rather than a prophet; Malik's repeated title الحكيم in the Muwatta reflects that Medinan scholarly reputation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p148/r3.anchor: فالجمهور قالوا : كان حكيما صالحا . واعتمد مالك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p148/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p148/r4.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p148/r4.claim: Ibn Umar reports a Prophetic hadith that Luqman was no prophet but a servant of much reflection and firm conviction who loved God and was granted wisdom.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p148/r4.anchor: ابن عمر قال : سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p148/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p148/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p148/r5.claim: Ibn Ashur judges Luqman was not a prophet: the story mentions no revelation or angels, calls his gift wisdom, and describes his instruction as counsel rather than legislation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p148/r5.anchor: ويظهر من الآيات المذكورة في قصته هذه أنه لم يكن نبيئا لأنه لم يمتن عليه بوحي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p148/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p148/r6.speaker: عكرمة والشعبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p148/r6.claim: Ikrima and al-Shabi hold that Luqman was a prophet; they argue that wisdom can denote prophethood, as with David and in 2:269, and that placing God's instruction about parents within Luqman's counsel supports this view.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p148/r6.anchor: وذهب عكرمة والشعبي : أن لقمان نبيء ولفظ الحكمة يسمح بهذا القول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p154/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p154/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p154/r1.claim: بني is a diminutive of ابن with the speaker's possessive ending; its spelling and case ending reflect restoration and merging of the original root letters and omission of the vocative possessive yā.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p154/r1.anchor: مضافا إلى ياء المتكلم فلذلك كسرت الياء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p154/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p154/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p154/r2.claim: Most readers pronounce بني with a doubled yā carrying kasra; Hafs from Asim reads it in the three occurrences in this surah with a doubled yā carrying fatḥa, as if from بنيا.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p154/r2.anchor: وقرأه الجمهور بكسر ياء { بني } مشددة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p154/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p154/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p154/r3.claim: The diminutive lovingly treats even an adult as a child, signaling compassion and sincere care in counsel and encouraging compliance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p154/r3.anchor: والتصغير فيه لتنزيل المخاطب الكبير منزلة الصغير كناية عن الشفقة به والتحبب له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p154/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p154/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p154/r4.claim: Luqman begins by removing shirk before seeking moral growth because sound belief is the foundation of sound action; rejecting shirk affirms one God and denies partners.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p154/r4.anchor: ابتدأ لقمان موعظة ابنه بطلب إقلاعه عن الشرك بالله لأن النفس المعرضة للتزكية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p347#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p347#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p347#2/r10.claim: Idh qāla may mean remember when Luqman said it, or We granted him wisdom when he said it; the wording is shortened because the preceding context makes it clear.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p347#2/r10.anchor: وقوله وإذ قال يحتمل أن يكون التقدير واذكر إذ قال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p347#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p347#2/r12.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p347#2/r12.claim: These readers double the yāʾ and give it kasra in the three occurrences of yā bunayya; Hafs and al-Mufaḍḍal from ʿAsim double it with fatḥa.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p347#2/r12.anchor: وقرأ نافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p347#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p347#2/r13.speaker: ابن أبي برة عن ابن كثير وقنبل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p347#2/r13.claim: Ibn Abi Barra reports Ibn Kathir with a silent yāʾ in the first occurrence, kasra in the second, and fatḥa in the third; Qunbul reports silence in the first and third and kasra in the second.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p347#2/r13.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي برة عن ابن كثير «يا بني» بسكون الياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p347#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p347#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p347#2/r14.claim: The warning that shirk is grave injustice may be Luqman's own speech or a divine statement attached to it; the report about 6:82 supports the latter and says it calmed the Companions' alarm.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p347#2/r14.anchor: وظاهر قوله إن الشرك لظلم عظيم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p348/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p348/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p348/r1.claim: The Companions' concern could be eased if the phrase were God's own statement; it could also be eased by God quoting a servant already described as wise and sound.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p348/r1.anchor: وإنما يسكن إشفاقهم بأن يكون ذلك خبرا من الله تعالى، وقد يسكن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p336/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p336/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p336/r1.claim: Luqman, whom God honored for wisdom, advises his beloved son first to worship God alone and warns that associating partners with Him is the greatest injustice; the son is named Tharan in a report cited by al-Suhaylī.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p336/r1.anchor: فهو حقيق أن يمنحه أفضل ما يعرف؛ ولهذا أوصاه أولا بأن يعبد الله وحده

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p336/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p336/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p336/r2.claim: When 6:82 troubled the Companions because they thought it condemned all wrongdoing, the Prophet explained that it meant shirk, citing Luqman's saying that shirk is a great injustice; Bukhārī and Muslim transmit it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p336/r2.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "أنه ليس بذاك، ألا (3) تسمع إلى قول لقمان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p336/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p336/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p336/r3.claim: Worship of God alone is paired with kindness to parents, as in 17:23 and often elsewhere in the Quran.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p336/r3.anchor: وكثيرا ما يقرن تعالى بين ذلك في القرآن

JISHUMI:v8p5649/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5649/r1.speaker: ابن كثير
JISHUMI:v8p5649/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr has several transmitted vocalizations for “my son”; the author identifies one as the relied-upon set and notes the many variants.
JISHUMI:v8p5649/r1.anchor: وعن ابن كثير في مثل ذلك آثار جمة، والمعتمد ما ذكرنا

JISHUMI:v8p5649/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5649/r2.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
JISHUMI:v8p5649/r2.claim: Ḥafṣ opens the yāʾ of “my son” throughout the Qur'an; the other readers use kasra. Sukun follows the original form, fatḥa drops the possessive after three yāʾs, and kasra is close to the possessive form.
JISHUMI:v8p5649/r2.anchor: أما السكون: فلأنه الأصل كما لو وقف، وأما الفتح: فعلى حذف الإضافة

JISHUMI:v8p5649/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5649/r7.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v8p5649/r7.claim: “When Luqman said to his son” coordinates with the account of wisdom, as if he was given wisdom when commanded to thank God and when admonishing his son; “while admonishing him” is circumstantial accusative.
JISHUMI:v8p5649/r7.anchor: كأنه قيل: آتيناه الحكمة إذ أمرناه بالشكر، وإذ قال لقمان لابنه واعظا له

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p500#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p500#2/r1.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p500#2/r1.claim: One report names Luqman's son An'am.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p500#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p500#2/r2.speaker: الكلبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p500#2/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi instead gives Luqman's son's name as Ashkam.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p500#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p500#2/r3.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p500#2/r3.claim: Another report says Luqman's son and wife were unbelievers, but Luqman kept persuading them until they accepted Islam.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p500#2/r3.anchor: وقيل : كان ابنه وامرأته كافرين ، فما زال بهما حتى أسلما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p500#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p500#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p500#2/r4.claim: Shirk is an immense injustice because it equates the sole giver of blessings with one who gives none and cannot give any; the enormity is beyond conception.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p500#2/r4.anchor: لأن التسوية بين من لا نعمة إلا هي منه ، ومن لا نعمة منه البتة ولا يتصور أن تكون منه ظلم

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p333/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p333/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p333/r1.claim: Muhammad is told to recall Luqman's admonition to his son; the son is variously named Mishkam, An'am, or Baban.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p333/r1.anchor: وفي اسم ابنه ثلاثة أقاويل : أحدها : مشكم , قاله الكلبي . الثاني : أنعم , حكاه النقاش

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p333/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p333/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p333/r2.claim: Luqman was reminding and disciplining his son; calling him يا بني conveys tenderness, not literal diminutiveness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p333/r2.anchor: يا بني } ليس هو حقيقة التصغير

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p333/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p333/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p333/r3.claim: Shirk is immense injustice because the idolater wrongs himself before God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p333/r3.anchor: يعني عند الله , وسماه ظلما لأنه قد ظلم به نفسه

MUJAHID:v2p507/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p507/r1.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
MUJAHID:v2p507/r1.claim: He reports that the sage Luqman worked as a tailor.
MUJAHID:v2p507/r1.anchor: عن سعيد ابن المسيب قال كان لقمان الحكيم خياطا

MUQATIL:31:12-13/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:31:12-13/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:31:12-13/r2.claim: Luqman’s son was named Anʿum; he counseled him against shirk, the gravest injustice, and his son and wife eventually became Muslim through persistence.
MUQATIL:31:12-13/r2.anchor: وإذ قال لقمان لابنه } واسم ابنه أنعم { وهو يعظه } يعنى عز وجل يؤدبه

MUQATIL:31:12-13/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:31:12-13/r3.speaker: قتادة بن دعامة
MUQATIL:31:12-13/r3.claim: Qatada reports that Luqman was flat-nosed and from Abyssinia.
MUQATIL:31:12-13/r3.anchor: عن قتادة بن دعامة، قال: كان لقمان رجلا أفطس من أرض الحبشة،

MUQATIL:31:12-13/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:31:12-13/r4.speaker: الهذيل
MUQATIL:31:12-13/r4.claim: Hudhayl says he did not hear Muqatil report the preceding description.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#2/r1.claim: اذكر إذ means remember when Luqmān admonished his son.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ وإذ ﴾ أى واذكر إذ ﴿ قال لقمان لابنه ﴾ أنعم أو اشكر

NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#2/r2.claim: The phrase beginning أنعم أو اشكر is given as another wording or interpretation in the exhortation to his son.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#2/r2.anchor: ﴿ قال لقمان لابنه ﴾ أنعم أو اشكر

NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#2/r3.speaker: مكي
NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#2/r3.claim: Makki reads yā bunayya with sukūn.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#2/r3.anchor: الاسكان مكى يا بنى حفض بفتحه فى كل القرآن

NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#2/r4.speaker: حفص
NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#2/r4.claim: Ḥafṣ reads yā bunayya with fatḥa throughout the Qurʾān.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#2/r4.anchor: يا بنى حفض بفتحه فى كل القرآن

NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#2/r5.claim: Associating partners is great injustice because it equates the One who supplies every blessing with beings that provide none.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p282#2/r5.anchor: لأنه تسوية بين من لا نعمة الا وهى منه ومن لا نعمة له أصلا

QURTUBI-FULL:6:81-82/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:81-82/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:6:81-82/r7.claim: When the Companions feared that every wrong disqualified them, the Prophet explained the verse by citing Luqman's statement that associating partners with God is grave injustice.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:81-82/r7.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: ليس هو كما تظنون إنما هو كما قال لقمان لابنه

QURTUBI-FULL:31:13/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:13/r1.speaker: السهيلي
QURTUBI-FULL:31:13/r1.claim: Al-Suhaylī says Luqmān's son was called Thārān according to al-Ṭabarī and al-Qutbī.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:13/r1.anchor: اسم ابنه ثاران في قول الطبري والقتبي

QURTUBI-FULL:31:13/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:13/r2.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:31:13/r2.claim: Al-Kalbī names Luqmān's son as Mishkam.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:13/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:13/r3.speaker: النقاش
QURTUBI-FULL:31:13/r3.claim: Al-Naqqāsh transmits another name for the son: Anʿam.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:13/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:13/r4.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:31:13/r4.claim: Al-Qushayrī says Luqmān's son and wife were unbelievers, and he continued admonishing them until they accepted Islam.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:13/r4.anchor: أن ابنه وامرأته كانا كافرين فما زال يعظهما حتى أسلما

QURTUBI-FULL:31:13/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:13/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:13/r5.claim: The admonition against associating partners with God supports the claim that Luqmān was instructing his son.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:13/r5.anchor: قلت: ودل على هذا قوله: { لا تشرك بالله إن الشرك لظلم عظيم }

QURTUBI-FULL:31:13/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:13/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:31:13/r6.claim: When 6:82 was revealed, the Companions feared that any wrongdoing invalidated their faith; the Prophet clarified that the verse's ظلم means shirk, as Luqmān told his son.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:13/r6.anchor: ليس هو كما تظنون إنما هو كما قال لقمان لابنه

QURTUBI-FULL:31:13/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:13/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:13/r7.claim: Scholars differ whether the statement that shirk is grave injustice is Luqmān's words or a divine comment joined to them; the reported revelation supports the latter, though either attribution could reassure the Companions.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:13/r7.anchor: واختلف في قوله: { إن الشرك لظلم عظيم } فقيل: إنه من كلام لقمان

QURTUBI-FULL:31:13/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:13/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:13/r8.claim: The particle idh is accusative as an instruction to remember; al-Zajjāj instead attaches it to āṯaynā, but al-Naḥḥās considers that mistaken because the intervening wāw prevents it.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:13/r8.anchor: النحاس: وأحسبه غلطا لأن في الكلام واوا تمنع من ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:31:13/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:13/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:13/r9.claim: The address yā bunayya is read with kasra on the yāʾ to indicate an omitted yāʾ; some use fatḥa as lighter. Its diminutive form expresses tenderness, not literal smallness.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:13/r9.anchor: وقوله: «يا بني» ليس هو على حقيقة التصغير وإن كان على لفظه

SAMIN-DURR:31:13/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:13/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:31:13/r1.claim: The governing element for إذ is omitted, وهو يعظه is circumstantial, and يا بني has earlier been discussed for variant readings.
SAMIN-DURR:31:13/r1.anchor: والعامل في " إذ " مضمر. " وهو يعظه " جملة حالية. " يا بني " قد تقدم خلاف القراء فيه

RAZI-FULL:v25p128/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p128/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p128/r4.claim: Luqman begins with the most important counsel, forbidding associationism because it is grave injustice.
RAZI-FULL:v25p128/r4.anchor: وفي هذا لطيفة وهي أن الله ذكر لقمان وشكر سعيه حيث أرشد ابنه ليعلم منه فضيلة النبي عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v25p128/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p128/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p128/r5.claim: Shirk wrongs the honored human by directing worship to a base object or by placing worship where it does not belong; it is uniquely grave because no one besides God can be worshipped.
RAZI-FULL:v25p128/r5.anchor: وأما الإشراك فوضع المعبودية في غير الله تعالى ولا يجوز أن يكون غيره معبودا أصلا

STUDYQURAN:31:13/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:31:13/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:31:13/r1.claim: Luqmān’s warning against associating partners and the divine charge to honor parents jointly guard against two gravest sins.
STUDYQURAN:31:13/r1.anchor: combined with the “charge”given to human beings about parents constitute protection against the two

STUDYQURAN:31:13/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:31:13/r2.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:31:13/r2.claim: The Prophet identifies associating partners with God and disrespecting parents among the greatest major sins.
STUDYQURAN:31:13/r2.anchor: the Prophet asked his Companions, “Shall I tell you what are the greatest of major sins? . . . To attribute partners to God

TAB-FULL:v18p550/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p550/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p550/r1.claim: God tells Muhammad to recall Luqman's counsel to his son: do not associate partners with God, since shirk is a grave error in speech.

ZAJJAJ:v4p195#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p195#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p195#2/r1.claim: إذ is governed by ‘We gave Luqman wisdom’: God gave it to him when he admonished his son, since this admonition itself is wisdom.
ZAJJAJ:v4p195#2/r1.anchor:
موضع " إذ " نصب بقوله: (ولقد آتينا لقمان الحكمة)
أي ولقد آتينا لقمان الحكمة إذ قال، لأن هذه الموعظة حكمة.

ZAJJAJ:v4p195#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p195#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p195#2/r2.claim: Shirk is grave injustice because God alone gives life, death, provision, and blessings; assigning a blessing to another is placing it with the wrong giver.
ZAJJAJ:v4p195#2/r2.anchor: يعني أن الله هو المحيي المميت الرازق المنعم وحده لا شريك له فإذا أشرك به أحد غيره فذلك أعظم الظلم

ZAJJAJ:v4p195#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p195#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p195#2/r3.claim: The basic Arabic meaning of ظلم is putting something in the wrong place.
ZAJJAJ:v4p195#2/r3.anchor: وأصل الظلم في اللغة وضع الشيء في غير موضعه

TABATABAI:31:12-14/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:12-14/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:12-14/r8.claim: The greatness of an offense rises with the greatness of the one offended; associating partners with God is the greatest offense, and the unqualified description “great injustice” marks its incomparable gravity.
TABATABAI:31:12-14/r8.anchor: عظمة كل عمل بعظمة أثره وعظمة المعصية بعظمة المعصي فإن مؤاخذة العظيم عظيمة

TABATABAI:31:12-19#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:12-19#2/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:31:12-19#2/r4.claim: Al-Ṣādiq says Luqman counseled his son so forcefully that the son nearly split apart, then reminded him that the afterlife destination approaches nearer than the worldly home he leaves behind.
TABATABAI:31:12-19#2/r4.anchor: ثم قال أبو عبد الله عليه السلام في قول الله عز وجل { وإذ قال لقمان لابنه وهو يعظه يا بني لا تشرك بالله إن الشرك لظلم عظيم } قال فوعظ لقمان ابنه باثار حتى تفطر وانشق

TABATABAI:31:12-19#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:12-19#2/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:31:12-19#2/r5.claim: Luqman urges his son to sit close to scholars without disputing them, take only enough from worldly life, avoid excess that harms the afterlife, and fast desire without missing prayer, which God loves more.
TABATABAI:31:12-19#2/r5.anchor: يا بني جالس العلماء وزاحمهم بركبتيك ولا تجادلهم فيمنعوك، وخذ من الدنيا بلاغا ولا ترفضها فتكون عيالا على الناس

TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r1.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r1.claim: Luqman compares worldly life to a deep sea where many learned people perish: faith is the boat, trust the sail, and piety provisions; survival is by mercy, while drowning follows sin.
TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r1.anchor: يا بني إن الدنيا بحر عميق قد هلك فيها عالم كثير فاجعل سفينتك فيها الإيمان واجعل شراعها التوكل

TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r2.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r2.claim: He says early manners bear fruit later, and learning grows through attention, effort, and persistent seeking; knowledge becomes a beneficial habit inherited by those who follow.
TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r2.anchor: يا بني إن تأدبت صغيرا انتفعت به كبيرا ومن عنى بالأدب أهتم به، ومن اهتم به تكلف علمه

TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r3.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r3.claim: Give time each day to learning; avoid quarrelling with the obstinate or jurists, hostility to rulers, companionship with tyrants, the wicked, or the suspect, and guard knowledge like papers.
TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r3.anchor: واجعل في أيامك ولياليك وساعاتك نصيبا في طلب العلم فإنك لن تجد له تضييعا أشد من تركه

TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r4.claim: Luqman tells his son to fear God even with all humanity's good deeds and hope even with all humanity's sins; a believer has two balanced lights, fear and hope.
TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r4.anchor: لو استخرج قلب المؤمن يوجد فيه نوران نور للخوف ونور للرجاء لو وزنا لما رجح أحدهما على الآخر

TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r5.claim: He explains that faith, sincerity, obedience, fear, love, and following God's command confirm one another and culminate in God's pleasure and Paradise; rejecting God's pleasure makes His anger seem insignificant.
TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r5.anchor: فمن يؤمن بالله يصدق ما قال الله عز وجل ومن يصدق ما قال الله يفعل ما أمر الله

TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r6.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r6.claim: Luqman warns against relying on worldly life: God regards nothing as lower, yet its pleasures are not the obedient's reward and its hardships are not punishment for sinners.
TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r6.anchor: يا بني لا تركن إلى الدنيا ولا تشغل قلبك بها فما خلق الله خلقا هو أهون عليه منها

TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r7.speaker: لقمان
TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r7.claim: Asked for the core of his wisdom, Luqman answers that he does not undertake what has already been taken care of for him or neglect what has been entrusted to him.
TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r7.anchor: وفي قرب الأسناد هارون عن ابن صدقة عن جعفر عن أبيه عليه السلام قيل للقمان ما الذي أجمعت عليه من حكمتك؟

TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r8.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r8.claim: Luqman argues that one cannot escape sleep or prevent waking; because sleep resembles death and awakening resembles resurrection, the self is clearly under another's control.
TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r8.anchor: عن جابر عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال كان فيما وعظ به لقمان ابنه أن قال يا بني إن تك في شك من الموت

TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r9.speaker: لقمان
TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r9.claim: Another saying warns against getting too close and becoming distant, or staying away and being humiliated; animals love their kind, while people may fail to love their own kind.
TABATABAI:31:12-19#3/r9.anchor: وقال قال لقمان لابنه يا بني لا تقترب فيكون أبعد لك ولا تبعد فتهان

TABATABAI:31:12-19#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:12-19#4/r1.speaker: لقمان
TABATABAI:31:12-19#4/r1.claim: Luqman advises sharing knowledge only with those who seek it and avoiding the wicked: like tar, bad company stains; disputation invites insult, suspicious places invite accusation, and an uncontrolled tongue brings regret.
TABATABAI:31:12-19#4/r1.anchor: لا تنشر بزك إلا عند باغيه، وكما ليس بين الكبش والذئب خلة كذلك ليس بين البار والفاجر خلة

TABATABAI:31:12-19#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:12-19#4/r2.speaker: لقمان
TABATABAI:31:12-19#4/r2.claim: He counsels making many friends rather than one enemy, cultivating religion and good manners, serving the virtuous, fulfilling trusts, and avoiding a sinful heart behind a pious appearance.
TABATABAI:31:12-19#4/r2.anchor: يا بني صاحب مائة ولا تعاد واحدا، يا بني إنما هو خلاقك وخلقك فخلاقك دينك وخلقك بينك وبين الناس

TABATABAI:31:12-19#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:12-19#4/r3.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:31:12-19#4/r3.claim: Al-Ṣādiq portrays people who accumulate for children as leaving both wealth and heirs behind; a person is a hired servant who must do the assigned work to earn the promised wage.
TABATABAI:31:12-19#4/r3.anchor: وفي الكافي بإسناده عن يحيى بن عقبة الأزدي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال كان فيما وعظ به لقمان لابنه

TABATABAI:31:12-19#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:12-19#4/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:31:12-19#4/r4.claim: The world should be treated as a bridge crossed and left behind, not a green field where one fattens for slaughter; one was not commanded to build it up.
TABATABAI:31:12-19#4/r4.anchor: ولكن اجعل الدنيا بمنزلة قنطرة على نهر جزت عليها فتركتها ولم ترجع إليها آخر الدهر

TABATABAI:31:12-19#4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:12-19#4/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:31:12-19#4/r5.claim: At judgment one is asked about youth, lifespan, and how wealth was earned and spent; prepare answers, do not grieve worldly loss, and repent and act before death blocks further choice.
TABATABAI:31:12-19#4/r5.anchor: واعلم أنك ستسأل غدا إذا وقفت بين يدي الله عز وجل عن أربع شبابك فيما أبليته، وعمرك فيما أفنيته

TABATABAI:31:12-19#4/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:12-19#4/r6.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:31:12-19#4/r6.claim: Another report counsels patience, calm, and good character; even without resources for relatives, kindness and a cheerful face win good people and deter the wicked, while contentment and lack of greed bring worldly honor.
TABATABAI:31:12-19#4/r6.anchor: وفي البحار عن القصص بإسناده عن حماد عن الصادق عليه السلام قال قال لقمان يا بني إياك والضجر وسوء الخلق وقلة الصبر

TABRISI:31:11-14/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:11-14/r1.speaker: ابن كثير برواية البزي
TABRISI:31:11-14/r1.claim: Al-Bazzī's Ibn Kathīr transmission varies the ya in yā bunayya: sukūn in the prohibition, kasra in annahā, and fatḥa in the prayer command.
TABRISI:31:11-14/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير في رواية البزي يا بني لا تشرك بالله ساكنة الياء يا بني أنها مكسورة الياء

TABRISI:31:11-14/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:11-14/r2.speaker: القواس
TABRISI:31:11-14/r2.claim: The al-Qawwās transmission has sukūn in the prohibition and prayer vocatives, and kasra in annahā.
TABRISI:31:11-14/r2.anchor: وقرأ في رواية القواس يا بني لا تشرك يا بني أقم ساكنة الياء فيهما

TABRISI:31:11-14/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:11-14/r3.speaker: ابن فليح
TABRISI:31:11-14/r3.claim: Ibn Fulayḥ has sukūn in the first vocative, kasra in annahā, and fatḥa in the prayer vocative.
TABRISI:31:11-14/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن فليح يا بني لا تشرك يا بني أنها مكسورة الياء فيهما يا بني أقم مفتوحة الياء

TABRISI:31:11-14/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:11-14/r4.speaker: حفص
TABRISI:31:11-14/r4.claim: Ḥafṣ reads yā bunayya with fatḥa throughout the Qur'an; the remaining readers use kasra throughout.
TABRISI:31:11-14/r4.anchor: وقرأ حفص يا بني بفتح الياء في كل القرآن والباقون بكسر الياء في كل القرآن

TABRISI:31:11-14/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:11-14/r7.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:31:11-14/r7.claim: A reader who suppresses the yāʾ may be applying a pause form in connected speech, as in poetry that shortens jān for rhyme and then links it.
TABRISI:31:11-14/r7.anchor: من أسكن الياء في الوصل فإنه يجوز أن يكون على قول

TABRISI:31:11-14/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:11-14/r8.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:31:11-14/r8.claim: The kasra in yā bunayya annahā follows the form yā ghulāmi aqbil; fatḥa treats the added yāʾ as changed to an alif, like yā abati according to Abu ʿUthman.
TABRISI:31:11-14/r8.anchor: ومن قال: يا بني أنها فهو على قولك يا غلام أقبل

TABRISI:31:14/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:14/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:14/r5.claim: Remember when Luqman spoke to his son may attach either to the command to remember or to God's giving him wisdom.
TABRISI:31:14/r5.anchor: معناه واذكر يا محمد إذ قال لقمان لابنه

TABRISI:31:14/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:14/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:14/r6.claim: The diminutive bunayya expresses tenderness and compassion, not belittlement; Luqman warns his son not to associate anything with God in worship.
TABRISI:31:14/r6.anchor: أي لا تعدل بالله شيئا في العبادة

TABRISI:31:14/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:14/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:14/r7.claim: Shirk is grave injustice because injustice is withholding what is due: the polytheist denies God's due, knowledge of His oneness; it also ruins the self.
TABRISI:31:14/r7.anchor: أصل الظلم النقصان ومنع الواجب فمن أشرك بالله فقد منع ما وجب لله عليه

TABRISI:31:11-15/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:11-15/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:11-15/r1.claim: Luqman's master asked him to slaughter a sheep and bring its two best morsels; Luqman brought the heart and tongue, saying they are best when good and worst when bad.
TABRISI:31:11-15/r1.anchor: اذبح شاة فأتني بأطيب مضغتين منها فذبح شاة وأتاه بالقلب واللسان

TABRISI:31:11-15/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:11-15/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:11-15/r2.claim: Luqman warned that sitting too long on the toilet harms the liver, causes hemorrhoids, and heats the head; sit and rise gently, so the master wrote this wisdom on the privy door.
TABRISI:31:11-15/r2.anchor: طول الجلوس على الحاجة يفجع منه الكبد ويورث منه الباسور

TABRISI:31:11-15/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:11-15/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن دينار
TABRISI:31:11-15/r3.claim: On returning from travel, Luqman heard that his father, wife, sister, and brother had died; he responded respectively that he now controlled his affairs, renewed his bed, covered his nakedness, and had lost his support.
TABRISI:31:11-15/r3.anchor: قال عبد الله بن دينار: قدم لقمان من سفر فلقي غلامه

TABRISI:31:11-15/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:11-15/r4.speaker: لقمان
TABRISI:31:11-15/r4.claim: Asked who is worst, Luqman answered: one unconcerned that people see him doing wrong.
TABRISI:31:11-15/r4.anchor: أي الناس شر قال: الذي لا يبالي أن يراه الناس مسيئا

TABRISI:31:11-15/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:11-15/r5.speaker: لقمان
TABRISI:31:11-15/r5.claim: When someone called his face ugly, he asked whether the criticism was of the design or its designer.
TABRISI:31:11-15/r5.anchor: ما أقبح وجهك قال: تعتب على النقش أو على فاعل النقش

TABRISI:31:11-15/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:11-15/r6.speaker: لقمان
TABRISI:31:11-15/r6.claim: Luqman watched David forge armor, praised it as good battle clothing, and said silence is wisdom few practice; David affirmed that Luqman deserved his name.
TABRISI:31:11-15/r6.anchor: وقال: نعم لبوس الحرب أنت فقال: الصمت حكم وقليل فاعله

TABRISI:31:11-15/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:11-15/r7.speaker: لقمان
TABRISI:31:11-15/r7.claim: A counsel in Man lā yaḥḍuruhu al-faqīh likens the world to a deep sea where many perish: make faith the ship, trust in God its sail, and piety its provisions.
TABRISI:31:11-15/r7.anchor: يا بني إن الدنيا بحر عميق وقد هلك فيها عالم كثير فاجعل سفينتك فيها الإيمان

TABRISI:31:11-15/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:11-15/r8.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:31:11-15/r8.claim: Abu ʿAbdillah's travel counsel calls for necessary gear and medicine, agreeable companions except in sin, frequent consultation, smiling, sharing food, helping companions, silence, prayer, and generosity with mounts, water, and provisions.
TABRISI:31:11-15/r8.anchor: سافر بسيفك وخفك وعمامتك وخبائك وسقائك وخيوطك ومخرزك وتزود معك من الأدوية

TABRISI:31:11-15/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:11-15/r9.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:31:11-15/r9.claim: His counsel says to verify advice before deciding, help and work alongside companions, heed elders, answer requests graciously, stop and deliberate when lost, and distrust solitary strangers in the wilderness as possible scouts or devils.
TABRISI:31:11-15/r9.anchor: إذا تحيرتم في الطريق فانزلوا وإذا شككتم في القصد فقفوا وتوامروا

TABRISI:31:11-15#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:11-15#2/r1.speaker: لقمان
TABRISI:31:11-15#2/r1.claim: Travel counsel says pray as soon as prayer time begins, preferably in congregation; do not sleep on an animal except in a litter that lets the limbs relax, and feed it before yourself near home.
TABRISI:31:11-15#2/r1.anchor: إذا جاء وقت الصلاة فلا تؤخرها لشيء صلها واسترح منها فإنها دين

TABRISI:31:11-15#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:11-15#2/r2.speaker: لقمان
TABRISI:31:11-15#2/r2.claim: At a campsite choose pleasant, soft, grassy ground, pray two cycles before sitting, go far away for relieving yourself, then pray two and greet the place and its angelic residents when leaving.
TABRISI:31:11-15#2/r2.anchor: وإذا أردتم النزول فعليكم من بقاع الأرض بأحسنها لونا وألينها تربة وأكثرها عشبا

TABRISI:31:11-15#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:11-15#2/r3.speaker: لقمان
TABRISI:31:11-15#2/r3.claim: Give some food away before eating if possible; recite scripture while riding, praise God while working, pray when alone, avoid traveling through the whole night, and do not raise your voice on the road.
TABRISI:31:11-15#2/r3.anchor: وإن استطعت أن لا تأكل طعاما حتى تبتدىء فتتصدق منه فافعل

THALABI:v7p320/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p320/r16.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p320/r16.claim: The warning against arguing about God without knowledge was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, who claimed the angels were God's daughters.
THALABI:v7p320/r16.anchor: نزلت في النضر بن الحرث حين زعم أن الملائكة بنات الله

ASAD-NOTES:31:13#n13/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:31:13#n13/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:31:13#n13/r1.claim: The diminutive “my little son” is an idiomatic term of affection regardless of whether the son is young or grown.
ASAD-NOTES:31:13#n13/r1.anchor: a diminutive idiomatically expressive of endearment irrespective of whether the son is a child or a grown man

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p101#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p101#2/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p101#2/r1.claim: Abū Isḥāq parses idh as an accusative linked to God giving Luqmān wisdom: the wisdom was given when he admonished his son, since the admonition itself is wisdom.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p101#2/r1.anchor: أبو إسحاق: موضع إذ نصب بقوله: {ولقد آتينا لقمان الحكمة} أي: ولقد آتيناه الحكمة إذ قال لابنه؛ لأن هذه الموعظة حكمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p101#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p101#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p101#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes the admonition to concern God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p101#2/r2.anchor: وهو يعظه} قال ابن عباس: في الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p101#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p101#2/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p101#2/r3.claim: Muqātil says Luqmān’s son and wife were unbelievers, and he kept admonishing them until they became Muslims.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p101#2/r3.anchor: كان ابنه وامرأته كفارا فما زال بهم حتى أسلموا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p101#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p101#2/r4.speaker: ابن كثير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p101#2/r4.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads yā bunayya with a lightened, still yāʾ and sukūn, also reported for the address at the start of verse 17.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p101#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير: يا بني، مخففة # ساكنة الياء، وكذلك: {يا بني أقم الصلاة}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p101#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p101#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p101#2/r5.claim: He explains the reading as reducing the shadda after deleting the possessive yāʾ from the original three yāʾs; he considers other reading explanations preferable and says such lightening fits a verse-ending rhyme better.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p101#2/r5.anchor: الأصل: يا بنيي بثلاث ياءات، ثم تحذف ياء الإضافة كما يقال: يا غلام أقبل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p101#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p101#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p101#2/r6.claim: He defends treating the final yāʾ as still present in underlying grammar even when eased at a pause, citing a poetic form with the yāʾ of banī lightened and its non-restoration in the plural as evidence.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p101#2/r6.anchor: فالياء (¬2) من بني مخففة للوقف، والتقدير بني يا هذا، فلما وقف عليه أسكن وخفف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p101#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p101#2/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p101#2/r7.claim: He notes that the lightened reading is pronounced as though pause-form were carried into connected speech, as in the cited poetic examples.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p101#2/r7.anchor: فإن وصلها ساكنة فقد أجرى الوصل مجرى الوقف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p103/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p103/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p103/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says no sin is greater than associating a partner with God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p103/r1.anchor: ليس من الذنوب شيء أعظم من الشرك بالله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p103/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p103/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p103/r2.claim: Abū Isḥāq reasons that God alone gives life, death, sustenance, and blessings; assigning worship to another misplaces the blessing and is thus the greatest injustice.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p103/r2.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: يعني أن الله هو المحي المميت الرازق المنعم وحده لا شريك له، فإذا أشرك به أحدا غيره فذلك أعظم الظلم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p103/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p103/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p103/r3.claim: Linguistically, injustice is putting something somewhere it does not belong.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p103/r3.anchor: وأصل الظلم في اللغة: وضع الشيء في غير موضعه

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p673/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p673/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p673/r2.claim: Luqman warns his son against shirk because it wrongs and harms the person who commits it; Hasan says it diminishes oneself, and al-Suddi calls it a great sin.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p673/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p673/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p673/r3.claim: When 6:82 said believers had not mixed faith with injustice, the Companions asked who was free of injustice; 31:13 was revealed to identify shirk as the injustice meant.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p673/r3.anchor: وأينا لم يظلم؟ فنزلت هذه الآية

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p673/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p673/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p673/r4.claim: The Prophet describes three wrongs: shirk is unforgiven, sins between a servant and God may be forgiven, and wrongs between people are not left without reciprocal redress.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p673/r4.anchor: الظلم ثلاثة: فظلم لا يغفره الله

ELMALILI:31:12-14/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r12.claim: Luqman's counsel to his son provides an example of how he expressed gratitude for wisdom.
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r12.anchor: Bu taksimden sonra Lokman’ın şükrünü nasıl edâ ettiğine dair hikmet ve ahlâktan bir iki numûne zikrolunarak

ELMALILI:31:12-14/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r13.speaker: Râgıb
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r13.claim: Raghib defines waʿẓ as a deterrent accompanied by warning or fear.

ELMALILI:31:12-14/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r14.speaker: İmam Halil
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r14.claim: Khalil defines waʿẓ as recalling good in a way that softens the heart; Elmalılı judges this definition better.
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r14.anchor: İmam Halil ise kalbi inceltecek vechile hayrı hatırlatmak demiştir ki daha güzeldir

ELMALILI:31:12-14/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r15.claim: Shirk is injustice because it gives God's due to another and places worship outside its proper place.
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r15.anchor: Çünkü zulüm bir şeyi mevzi‘inin gayriye koymaktır. Allah’ın hakkını Allah’tan başkasına vermektir

ELMALILI:31:12-14/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r16.claim: Shirk also degrades the human soul, which God honored, by making it worship a created being.
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r16.anchor: Allah’ın mükerrem kıldığı, şeref verdiği nefs-i insânîyi mahlûka ibadet ettirerek tezlil eylemektir

ELMALILI:31:12-14/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r17.claim: Shirk is an especially grave injustice because no one besides God can ever rightly or possibly occupy the status of deity; unlike property, divine status cannot be transferred.
ELMALILI:31:12-14/r17.anchor: mâbudluğu Allah’ın mâsivâsına vermektir. Allah’ın mâsivâsının ise mâbud olmasına hiçbir vechile cevaz ve imkân yoktur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:12/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:12/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:12/r9.claim: Justice is essential to wisdom and means putting things in their proper place and giving everyone their due; shirk wrongfully assigns God's divinity to another and is the greatest injustice.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:12/r9.anchor: Allah’ın hakkı olan tanrılığı başkasına vermiş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:12/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:12/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:12/r10.claim: Islam's priority of eliminating shirk reflects the view that it heads all evils and causes many others.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:12/r10.anchor: İslâm’ın en başta şirki ortadan kaldırmayı hedeflemesi de Allah’a ortak koşmanın, bütün kötülüklerin başında geldiği

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p453#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p453#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p453#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir's Ibn Abi Bizza transmission uses silent yāʾ in يا بني لا تشرك, kasra in يا بني إنها, and fatḥa in يا بني أقم; Qunbul has silence in the first and third and kasra in the middle.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p453#2/r1.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير (يا بني لا تشرك بالله) [لقمان/ 13] بوقف الياء، و (يا بني إنها) مكسورة الياء

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p453#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p453#2/r2.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p453#2/r2.claim: Hafs from Asim reads all three يا بني forms with fatḥa; Abu Bakr from Asim, Nafi, Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, Hamza, and Kisai use kasra in the third form.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p453#2/r2.anchor: وروى حفص عن عاصم الثلاثة بفتح الياء فيهن. أبو بكر عن عاصم بكسر الياء في الثالثة، وكذلك قرأ نافع وأبو عمرو

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p453#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p453#2/r3.speaker: المفضل عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p453#2/r3.claim: Al-Mufaddal from Asim reads يا بني with fatḥa in all three cited places.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p453#2/r3.anchor: المفضل عن عاصم: يا بني نصب في الثلاثة المواضع .

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p453#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p453#2/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p453#2/r4.claim: A silent yāʾ in connected recitation extends a pause form into speech, an extension known in poetry but not ordinary speech; a kasra form is the normal vocative construction because the possessive yāʾ acts like tanwīn and drops.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p453#2/r4.anchor: وهذا لا نعلمه جاء في الكلام، ومن قال: (يا بني إنها) [لقمان/ 16] فهو على قولك: يا غلام أقبل

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p453#2/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p453#2/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p453#2/r5.claim: Fatḥa on the yāʾ comes from يا بنيا, replacing the possessive yāʾ with alif and changing kasra to fatḥa; Abu Uthman explains يا أبت similarly.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p453#2/r5.anchor: ومن قال: يا بني ففتح الياء، فإنه على قولك يا بنيا فأبدل من ياء الإضافة ألفا

QIRAAT-ER:31:13:11#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:31:13:11#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:31:13:11#1/r1.claim: Bunay has sukūn on the final yāʾ, a shorter and more compressed diminutive form.
QIRAAT-ER:31:13:11#1/r1.anchor: Sukūn on final yāʾ: bunay — a shorter diminutive form

QIRAAT-ER:31:13:11#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:31:13:11#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:31:13:11#2/r1.claim: Bunayyi has kasra on the final yāʾ, making the possessive marking more explicit.
QIRAAT-ER:31:13:11#2/r1.anchor: Kasra on final yāʾ: bunayyi — the possessive yāʾ (ī) is partially retained

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p412/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p412/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p412/r12.claim: The phrase describing Luqman’s son as “barr” is explained as beneficent or thankful.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p412/r12.anchor: وابنه بار، أي: أو أنعم، أو اشكر، أو شاكر، أقوال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p412/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p412/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p412/r13.claim: A report says Luqman’s son and wife were unbelievers, but he kept advising them until they accepted Islam.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p412/r13.anchor: قيل: كان ابنه وامرأته كافرين، فما زال يعظهما حتى أسلما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p412/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p412/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p412/r14.claim: The apparent reading makes “associating partners is a great injustice” part of Luqman’s speech; a separate divine statement is also proposed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p412/r14.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله: إن الشرك لظلم عظيم من كلام لقمان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p412/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p412/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p412/r15.claim: Muslim’s authentic collection contains a report that appears to treat the warning against shirk as Luqman’s own words.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p412/r15.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم ما ظاهره أنه من كلام لقمان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p412/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p412/r16.speaker: البزي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p412/r16.claim: Al-Bazzi reads “my dear son” with a quiescent yāʾ in the first occurrence, kasra in the middle, and fatḥa in the third.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p412/r16.anchor: وقرأ البزي: يا بني، بالسكون، ويا بني إنها: بكسر الياء، ويا بني أقم: بفتحها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p412/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p412/r17.speaker: حفص والمفضل عن عاصم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p412/r17.claim: Hafs and al-Mufaddal from Asim read the yāʾ with fatḥa in all three occurrences, treating it as “yā bunayya” with the alif elided.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p412/r17.anchor: وحفص والمفضل عن عاصم: بالفتح في الثلاثة على تقدير يا بنيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r1.claim: The remaining seven canonical readers use kasra in all three forms of “my dear son.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p413/r1.anchor: وقرأ باقي السبعة: بالكسر في الثلاثة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p64/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p64/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v21p64/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the sura was revealed in Mecca without exception; another report from him exempts three verses, 31:27–29, revealed in Medina after Jewish rabbis challenged the Prophet's statement that human knowledge is little compared with the Torah.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p64/r1.anchor: والبيهقي في الدلائل عن إبن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنه قال : أنزلت سورة لقمان بمكة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p64/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p64/r2.speaker: عطاء
ALUSI-FULL:v21p64/r2.claim: A report from Ata, also cited by al-Dani and Abu Hayyan from Qatada, calls the sura Meccan except for two verses beginning with the parable of trees and pens.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p64/r2.anchor: ونقل الداني عن عطاء وأبو حيان عن قتادة أنهما قالا : هي مكية إلا آيتين

ALUSI-FULL:v21p64/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p64/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p64/r3.claim: Another view makes the sura Meccan except for the verse about prayer and zakat because their obligation supposedly began in Medina; the author objects that prayer was prescribed in Mecca on the Night Journey and was at least enjoined there, so this argument fails.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p64/r3.anchor: وقيل : هي مكية إلا آية وهي قوله تعالى : ( الذين يقيمون الصلاة ويؤتون الزكاة )

ALUSI-FULL:v21p64/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p64/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p64/r4.claim: The claim about prayer and zakat could instead mean both obligations came into force in Medina, even if prayer was already prescribed in Mecca; or zakat may have been prescribed in Mecca, with its taxable thresholds fixed in Medina, which removes the argument.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p64/r4.anchor: فلعل ذلك القائل أراد أن إيجابهما معا تحقق بالمدينة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p64/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p64/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p64/r5.claim: The sura has thirty-three verses in Meccan and Medinan counting systems, and thirty-four in other systems.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p64/r5.anchor: وآيها ثلاث وثلاثون في المكي والمدني وأربع وثلاثون في عدد الباقين

ALUSI-FULL:v21p64/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p64/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p64/r6.claim: According to al-Bahr, Quraysh asked about Luqman's story with his son and dutifulness to parents, and the sura was revealed in response.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p64/r6.anchor: وسبب نزولها على ما في البحر أن قريشا سألت عن قصة لقمان

ALUSI-FULL:v21p64/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p64/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p64/r7.claim: Al-Bahr relates the sura's opening to the preceding statement that the Quran gives every sort of parable, echoed in this sura's opening, and to the earlier challenge to bring a sign, answered by the description of turning away proudly from God's signs.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p64/r7.anchor: ووجه مناسبتها لما قبلها على ما فيه أيضا أنه قال تعالى فيما قبل

ALUSI-FULL:v21p64/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p64/r8.speaker: السيوطي
ALUSI-FULL:v21p64/r8.claim: Al-Suyuti connects the two suras through their shared opening letters; Luqman's description of guidance, prayer, zakat, and certainty in the afterlife resumes the prior description of knowledgeable believers who affirm resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p64/r8.anchor: ظهر لي في إتصالها بما قبلها مع المؤاخاة في الإفتتاح بألمإن قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v21p65/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p65/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p65/r1.claim: The prior sura's believers are in a garden where they rejoice, interpreted as listening, while Luqman's sura begins with idle talk, interpreted as singing and instruments; the author promises a later discussion.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p65/r1.anchor: في روضة يحبرون ) وقد فسر بالسماع وذكر هنا ( ومن الناس من يشتري لهو الحديث

ALUSI-FULL:v21p65/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p65/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p65/r2.claim: The prior account of Rome and Persia concerns rulers fighting over a base worldly prize unworthy of a wise person; this sura instead presents Luqman, a wise enslaved man indifferent to worldly life, counseling his son against war and toward patience and peace.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p65/r2.anchor: وما ألطف هذا الإتصال من حيث أن السورة الأولى ذكر فيها مغلوبية الروم

ALUSI-FULL:v21p65/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p65/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p65/r3.claim: The suras also connect in teaching how easy resurrection is: one says God begins and repeats creation, and the other says creating and raising people is like making one soul; both affirm God's hearing and sight.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p65/r3.anchor: فيما تقدم قوله تعالى : ( وهو الذي يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده وهو أهون عليه )

ALUSI-FULL:v21p65/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p65/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p65/r4.claim: The previous sura says some people return to associating partners after hardship, while Luqman says people call upon God alone in storm waves and some later take a moderate course; each sura includes material absent from the other.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p65/r4.anchor: وإذا مس الناس ضر دعوا ربهم منيبين إليه ثم إذا أذاقهم منه رحمة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r1.speaker: الطبري
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r1.claim: Al-Tabari and al-Qutaybi give Luqman's son's name as Taran; other reports give Mathan, An'am, Ashkam, or Mishkam.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r1.anchor: تاران على ما قال الطبري والقتبي وقيل : ماثان بالمثلثة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r2.claim: The particle idh is governed by an omitted command to remember; alternatively it may modify God's grant of wisdom, with omitted words understood from the context.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r2.anchor: معمول لا ذكر محذوفا وقيل : يحتمل أن يكون ظرفا لآتينا

ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r3.claim: The phrase while he was exhorting him is a circumstantial clause; waʿẓ is deterrence joined with warning, or a reminder of good that softens the heart.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r3.anchor: والوعظكما قال الراغبزجر مقترن يتخويف وقال الخليل : هو التذكير بالخير

ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r4.claim: The affectionate diminutive ya bunayya expresses compassion and love rather than belittlement, as two cited poems illustrate.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r4.anchor: تصغير إشفاق ومحبة لا تصغير تحقير

ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r5.claim: Al-Bazzi reads ya bunayya with a silent yāʾ here, with kasra in a later occurrence and fatḥa in another; a variant gives the same first and third vowels and the middle kasra.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ البزي هنا ( يابني ) بالسكون وفيما بعد ( يابني إنها ) بكسر الياء

ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r6.claim: Hafs and al-Mufaddal read the three forms with fatḥa, treating the vowel as a substitute for the omitted alif in ya bunayya; the remaining seven readers use kasra.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r6.anchor: وحفص والمفضل عن عاصم بالفتح في الثلاثة على تقدير يابنيا

ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r7.claim: Some say Luqman's son was an unbeliever and he warned him until the son converted; a report from al-Fadl al-Raqqashi says Luqman advised him until he died.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r7.anchor: قيل : كان إبنه كافرا ولذا نهاه عن الشرك

ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r8.speaker: حفص بن عمر الكندي
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r8.claim: Hafs ibn Umar al-Kindi tells how Luqman placed mustard seeds in a bag, removing one for each lesson; when it ran out, he said his teaching would split a mountain, and his son wept.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r8.anchor: عن حفص بن عمر الكندي قال : وضع لقمان جرابا من خردل

ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r9.claim: Others say the son and Luqman's wife were already Muslim; the warning against shirk then cautions them against falling into it in future.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r9.anchor: وقيل : كان مسلما والنهي عن الشرك تحذير له عن صدوره منه في المستقبل

ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r10.claim: If one pauses after la tushrik, the following bi is an oath particle, making the phrase swear by God that associating partners is a grave wrong.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r10.anchor: ومن وقف على ( لا تشرك ) جعل الباء للقسم أي أقسم بالله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r11.claim: The declaration that shirk is a great wrong is most likely Luqman's own speech, as Muslim's Sahih supports; it explains the prohibition because shirk puts things out of place and equates God, the sole giver of blessing, with one who gives none.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r11.anchor: والظاهر أن هذا من كلام لقمان ويقتضيه كلام مسلم في صحيحه

ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r12.claim: Alternatively, the declaration is God's own words, detached from Luqman's speech but continuing to reinforce the warning.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p84#2/r12.anchor: وقيل : هو خير من الله تعالى شأنه منقطع عن كلام لقمان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p287/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p287/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p287/r1.claim: Luqman's son was called Anam, or, according to another report, Mashkam.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p287/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p287/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p287/r2.claim: For ya bunayya la tushrik, Ibn Kathir reads the yāʾ quiescent, Hafs with fatḥa, and the others with kasra; other ya bunayya forms in nearby counsel also vary by reader.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p287/r2.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير: "يا بني لا تشرك بالله" بإسكان الياء، وفتحها حفص، والباقون بالكسر،

BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r1.claim: The source gives several possible names for Luqman's son: Anʿam, Ashkam, or another uncertain name.
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r1.anchor: أنعم أو أشكم أو ما ثان.

BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r2.claim: Ya bunayya is a diminutive expressing tenderness; Ibn Kathir, Hafs, al-Bazzi, and other readers differ on its yāʾ vowel in the cited places.
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r2.anchor: تصغير إشفاق، وقرأ ابن كثير هنا وفي { يبنى أقم الصلوة } بإسكان الياء

BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r3.claim: One view says Luqman's son was a disbeliever whom his father advised until he became Muslim; stopping at lā tushrik makes bi-llāh an oath.
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r3.anchor: قيل كان كافرا فلم يزل به حتى أسلم، ومن وقف على { لا تشرك } جعل بالله قسما.

BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r4.claim: Shirk is grave injustice because it equates the one who alone bestows blessings with one who bestows none.
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r4.anchor: لأنه تسوية بين من لا نعمة إلا منه ومن لا نعمة منه.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p13/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p13/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p13/r1.claim: Luqmān’s story recalls his gratitude in himself and his instruction of his son; repudiating shirk is the highest gratitude, and his example teaches patience, thankfulness, persistence in good, and child-rearing.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p13/r1.anchor: ما يدل على شكره في نفسه وأمره به لغيره فإنه لا شكر يعدل البراءة من الشرك

BIQAI-FULL:v6p13/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p13/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p13/r2.claim: Luqmān admonishes his son with counsel that benefits, softens the heart, disciplines the soul, and produces reverence and justice; the wording suggests repeated admonition.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p13/r2.anchor: أي يوصيه بما ينفعه ويرقق قلبه ويهذب نفسه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p13/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p13/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p13/r3.claim: The affectionate address ‘my son’ expresses tenderness and compassion to make the counsel more acceptable.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p13/r3.anchor: بأحب ما يخاطب به , مع إظهار الترحم والتحنن والشفقة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p13/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p13/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p13/r4.claim: Correct belief comes before sound action; the prohibition covers both manifest and hidden forms of associating partners with God.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p13/r4.anchor: أي لا توقع الشرك لا جليا ولا خفيا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p13/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p13/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p13/r5.claim: Shirk is grave injustice because it puts things out of place, especially by equating a dependent creature with the Necessary Being, from whom every blessing comes; it contradicts wisdom.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p13/r5.anchor: أي فهو ضد الحكمة , لأنه وضع الشيء في غير محله

BIQAI-FULL:v6p13/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p13/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p13/r6.claim: The counsel warns Quraysh and every listener that a wise father would not depart from it; its consequence is security and guidance, the great religious and worldly blessings.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p13/r6.anchor: وفي هذا تنبيه لقريش وكل سامع على أن هذه وصية لا يعدل عنها

BIQAI-FULL:v6p14/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p14/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
BIQAI-FULL:v6p14/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that the Companions were distressed by the ‘injustice’ in 6:82; the Prophet explained it by citing Luqmān’s statement that shirk is grave injustice. The author calls the report sound in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p14/r1.anchor: كما هو صحيح البخاري في غير موضع عن عبدالله بن مسعود

QUSHAYRI:v3p16#2/r25.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p16#2/r25.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p16#2/r25.claim: Shirk is divided into overt idolatry and hidden shirk, which includes attributing events to created people or affirming another alongside God while witnessing the unseen.
QUSHAYRI:v3p16#2/r25.anchor: الشرك على ضربين : جلي وخفي ؛ فالجلي عبادة الأصنام ، والخفي حسبان شيء من الحدثان من الأنام

QUSHAYRI:v3p16#2/r26.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p16#2/r26.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p16#2/r26.claim: Another definition calls shirk affirming anything other than God while witnessing the unseen.
QUSHAYRI:v3p16#2/r26.anchor: ويقال الشرك إثبات غير مع شهود الغيب

QUSHAYRI:v3p16#2/r27.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p16#2/r27.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p16#2/r27.claim: Shirk wrongs the heart, whereas sins wrong the self; wrongs of the self may be forgiven, but there is no avenue to forgiveness for wronging the heart.
QUSHAYRI:v3p16#2/r27.anchor: ويقال الشرك ظلم على القلب ، والمعاصي ظلم على النفس ، وظلم النفوس معرض للغفران

BURHAN:v2p183/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p183/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p183/r1.claim: Qur'anic verses divide into those clear by themselves and those requiring explanation; many examples of the first kind are listed.
BURHAN:v2p183/r1.anchor: ما هو بين بيفسه بلفظ لا يحتاج إلى بيان

BURHAN:v2p183/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p183/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURHAN:v2p183/r4.claim: A report in both Ṣaḥīḥ collections says the Prophet, answering Ibn Masʿūd's companions, explained zulm in 6:82 as shirk and cited Luqman's words in 31:13.
BURHAN:v2p183/r4.anchor: قالوا يا رسول الله وأينا لا يظلم نفسه قال ليس ذلك إنما هو الشرك ألم تسمعوا ما قال لقمان لابنه

BURHAN:v3p42/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p42/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p42/r5.claim: Some parse the bāʾ in “do not associate with God” as an oath, supplying an omitted لا تشرك before بالله; most omitted-verb oaths use wāw instead.
BURHAN:v3p42/r5.anchor: وقال الباء باء القسم وليست متعلقة تشرك وكأنه يقول

ITQAN:v1p229#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p229#2/r1.speaker: ابن الجزري
ITQAN:v1p229#2/r1.claim: Ibn al-Jazari says a reader should seek the fullest meaning and soundest pause, not adopt strained stopping or starting to force an interpretation; he gives several such examples, including splitting the final prayer into a vocative.
ITQAN:v1p229#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن الجزري أيضا ليس كلما يتعسفه بعض المعربين أو يتكلفه بعض القراء أو يتأوله بعض أهل الأهواء

ITQAN:v4p462#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p462#2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p462#2/r3.claim: When the Companions asked who had never wronged himself, the Prophet explained that the wrong in 6:82 means associating partners with God, citing Luqman 31:13.
ITQAN:v4p462#2/r3.anchor: ففسره النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم واستدل عليه بقوله ﴿ إن الشرك لظلم عظيم ﴾

ITQAN:v4p391/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p391/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p391/r7.claim: Luqman's son is called Baran, Daran, Anʿam, or Mashkam.
ITQAN:v4p391/r7.anchor: إسمه باران بالموحدة وقيل داران وقيل أنعم وقيل مشكم

ITQAN:v4p352/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p352/r1.speaker: غيره
ITQAN:v4p352/r1.claim: A cited grammarian says Qur'anic oaths with an omitted verb normally use واو; when باء appears the verb is stated, so readings that make phrases such as بالله إن الشرك لظلم an oath are mistaken.
ITQAN:v4p352/r1.anchor: وقال غيره أكثر الأقسام في القرآن المحذوفة الفعل لا تكون إلا بالواو فإذا ذكرت الباء أتي بالفعل

ITQAN:v4p352/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p352/r2.speaker: ابن القيم
ITQAN:v4p352/r2.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim says God swears by Himself or His signs; oaths by created things show their greatness as signs. The Qur'an's oaths affirm core beliefs, revelation, messengership, judgment, promise, warning, and human condition.
ITQAN:v4p352/r2.anchor: وقال ابن القيم اعلم أنه سبحانه وتعالى يقسم بأمور على أمور وإنما يقسم بنفسه المقدسة الموصوفة بصفاته

ITQAN:v4p352/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p352/r3.speaker: ابن القيم
ITQAN:v4p352/r3.claim: An oath may accompany a declarative statement, most commonly, or an imperative; it can confirm the asserted matter or the oath itself, and its response may be stated or omitted when understood.
ITQAN:v4p352/r3.anchor: وإما على جملة طلبية كقوله ﴿ فوربك لنسألنهم أجمعين عما كانوا يعملون ﴾ مع أن هذا القسم قد يراد به تحقيق المقسم عليه

ITQAN:v4p508/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p508/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p508/r2.claim: When companions worried about mixing faith with wrongdoing, Ibn Masud reports the Prophet clarifying that the verse means shirk, citing Luqman's statement that associationism is great injustice.
ITQAN:v4p508/r2.anchor: وأخرج أحمد والشيخان وغيرهم عن ابن مسعود قال لما نزلت هذه الآية ﴿ الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p371/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p371/r1.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p371/r1.claim: Ibn Qutayba describes shirk linguistically as a verbal noun meaning to partner with someone in a matter.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p371/r1.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة : الشرك في اللغة : مصدر شركته في الأمر أشركه .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p371/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p371/r2.speaker: معاذ
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p371/r2.claim: The entry cites a hadith report that Muadh permitted partnership among people of Yemen.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p371/r2.anchor: وفي الحديث : ' إن معاذا أجاز بين أهل اليمن الشرك

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p371/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p371/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p371/r3.claim: In sharecropping, shirk can mean two or three people entering into a partnership.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p371/r3.anchor: ويراد في المزارعة أن يشترك فيها رجلان أو ثلاثة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p371/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p371/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p371/r4.claim: Shirk with God means assigning Him a partner.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p371/r4.anchor: وإن الشرك بالله هو : أن يجعل له شريك .

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p258/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p258/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p258/r1.claim: The basic Arab sense of ẓulm is placing something outside its proper place; common expressions apply it to resemblance, premature drinking, needless slaughter, wrongly dug land, and leaving a road.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p258/r1.anchor: في كلام العرب: وضع الشيء في غير موضعه

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p258/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p258/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p258/r2.claim: Ẓulm can mean shirk because assigning God a partner places lordship where it does not belong; this is also the sense of the cited verse in al-Anʿām.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p258/r2.anchor: ثم قد يصير الظلم بمعنى الشرك، لأن من جعل لله شريكا: فقد وضع الربوبية غير موضعها

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p258/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p258/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p258/r3.claim: Ẓulm also means diminution or withholding: the cited phrases about crops, rights, and souls mean that nothing was reduced or withheld.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p258/r3.anchor: ويكون الظلم: النقصان، قال الله تعالى

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p258/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p258/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p258/r4.claim: Ẓulm can mean denial: the Thamūd denied that the she-camel was from God, and “wronging Our signs” means denying them.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p258/r4.anchor: ويكون الظلم: الجحد، قال الله تعالى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p97/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p97/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p97/r2.claim: Luqman’s wisdom is practical as well as verbal: personally tending and advising his son models parents’ duty to guide children instead of leaving them to bad teachers or the streets.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p97/r2.anchor: حكمة لقمان ليست فيما ذكره من أحاديث وأقوال وما قاله لابنه من الوصية، وإنما أيضا في العمل الذي فعله

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p99/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p99/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p99/r1.claim: The diminutive يا بني expresses endearment; Luqman begins gently rather than with rebuke or scolding.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p99/r1.anchor: كلمة تصغير للتحبيب، أي ابدأ بالكلام اللين اللطيف الهين للابن وليس بالتعنيف والزجر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p99/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p99/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p99/r2.claim: A gentle word opens a child's heart and makes the child receptive; the author connects this approach to God's instruction that Moses and Aaron speak gently to Pharaoh.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p99/r2.anchor: الكلمة الطيبة الهينة اللينة تفتح القلوب المقفلة وتلين النفوس العصية، عكس الكلمة الشديدة المنفرة التي تقفل النفوس

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p99/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p99/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p99/r3.claim: Sitting beside a child, placing a hand on his head or shoulder, and addressing him tenderly can affect him more than a long explanation and remove barriers to listening.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p99/r3.anchor: وأنت أيها الأب إن أجلست ولدك إلى جانبك ووضعت يدك على رأسه وكتفه، وقلت له يا بني، فتأكد أن هذه الكلمة بل هذه الحركة من المسح تؤثر أضعاف الكلام

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p99/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p99/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p99/r4.claim: The author recommends gentle, non-coercive parenting because a soft word can achieve more than a harsh one; he recounts telling his own son that gentleness had earned him more than his due.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p99/r4.anchor: تعلمت أنه بالكلمة الهينة اللينة آخذ أكثر من حقي

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p98/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p98/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p98/r1.claim: The wisdom introduction portrays Luqman as practicing what he teaches: advice is ineffective if its giver contradicts it in action.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p98/r1.anchor: فهل من الحكمة أن يوصي ابنه بشيء ويخالفه؟ هذا ليس من الحكمة ولو فعله فلن تنفع وصيته

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p98/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p98/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p98/r2.claim: Luqman's example teaches parents to take responsibility for their child's upbringing and education rather than leave the child to bad or ignorant influences.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p98/r2.anchor: الثاني في تعهده لابنه وتربيته وتعليمه وعدم تركه لأهل السوء والجهالة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p98/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p98/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p98/r3.claim: Preachers, advisers, and parents should begin by applying their own counsel; otherwise their words lose force.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p98/r3.anchor: أن يبدؤوا بأنفسهم فإن ذلك من الحكمة وإلا سقطت جميع أقوالهم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p98/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p98/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p98/r4.claim: The circumstantial construction suggests continuity and that Luqman chose a time when his son was ready to receive counsel.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p98/r4.anchor: من حيث اللغة: الحال والاستئناس للدلالة على الاستمرار. وهو يعظه اختار الوقت المناسب للوعظ

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p98/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p98/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p98/r5.claim: This was Luqman's regular care for his son, not a one-time admonition; educators should continue to guide those in their care.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p98/r5.anchor: فهذا من شأن لقمان أن يعظ ابنه، هو لا يتركه، وليست هذه هي المرة الأولى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p98/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p98/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p98/r6.claim: The affectionate address يا بني models gentleness in admonition.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p100/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p100/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p100/r1.claim: Luqmān begins by forbidding shirk because tawḥīd is the foundation of religion and worship is not accepted alongside shirk; it is the most important matter.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p100/r1.anchor: التوحيد أس الأمور، ولا تقبل عبادة مع الشرك، فالتوحيد أهم شيء

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p100/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p100/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p100/r2.claim: Tawḥīd should be taught from childhood because beliefs learned young are difficult to uproot; it remains needed in adulthood, while worship duties begin after legal maturity.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p100/r2.anchor: التوحيد تعلمه الصغير والكبير، فالمعتقدات تُتعلم في الصغر وما تعلم في الصغر فمن الصعب فيما بعد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p100/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p100/r3.speaker: author
