SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p100/r3.claim: The prohibition of shirk is broader and easier than the burden of worship, so Luqmān begins with the requirement that applies to young and old before the heavier acts of worship.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p100/r3.anchor: الأمر بعدم الشرك (أي بالتوحيد) هو أيسر من التكليف بالعبادة، العبادة ثقيلة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p100/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p100/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p100/r4.claim: Shirk is called grave injustice because equating a capable, knowledgeable candidate with an incompetent one is unfair; the disparity between Creator and created object of worship is far greater.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p100/r4.anchor: الفرق بين الله وبين المعبود الآخر أكبر بكثير، ليست هناك نسبة بين الخالق والمخلوق

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p106/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p106/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p106/r3.claim: Luqman’s counsel shows Arabs that their own sages taught what the Qur’an teaches; it contrasts blind imitation of forefathers who followed Satan with the wise ancestors’ reflection, and condemns punishing children for conduct Luqman taught his son.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p106/r3.anchor: The succeeding verses refer to the wisdom of Luqmān and the advise he gave to his obedient son.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p107/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p107/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p107/r4.claim: The author infers that Luqmān gave this counsel when his son was being crowned the next tribal chief.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p107/r4.anchor: they were imparted to him at the time when he was being crowned as the next tribal chief.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p109/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p109/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p109/r1.claim: The essence of gratitude is avoiding polytheism: since God grants all favors, thanks to others are subordinate to thanks to Him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p109/r1.anchor: similarly the true essence of gratitude is abstinence from polytheism.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p109/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p109/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p109/r2.claim: Associating others with God usurps His greatest right and is therefore the greatest injustice.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p109/r2.anchor: he is guilty of usurping the greatest of rights – and there is nothing more unjust than this.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p109/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p109/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p109/r3.claim: Luqmān delivered this counsel deliberately and elaborately on a specific occasion, stressing that his son should adhere to it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p109/r3.anchor: they were said on a specific occasion in an elaborate way as advice to his son

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p109/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p109/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p109/r4.claim: The Qur’ān directs its audience to compare what a wise father teaches his son with how they themselves treat their children.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p109/r4.anchor: The purpose is to direct the attention of the addressees of the Qur’ān what a wise father teaches his son

NASHR:v1p230/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p230/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p230/r4.claim: Readers should seek the fullest coherent meaning rather than contrived stops produced by grammarians, reciters, or partisan interpreters; the cited examples create misleading syntax or theology.
NASHR:v1p230/r4.anchor: بل ينبغي تحري المعنى الأتم والوقف الأوجه، وذلك نحو الوقف على وارحمنا أنت

NASHR:v1p230/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p230/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p230/r7.claim: Do not stop after لقمان’s لا تشرك and begin بالله إن الشرك as an oath; that forced break corrupts the sense.
NASHR:v1p230/r7.anchor: وإذ قال لقمان لابنه وهو يعظه يابني لا تشرك ثم الابتداء بالله إن الشرك

NASHR:v2p289/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p289/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p289/r1.claim: Ḥafṣ opens the yāʾ in all six occurrences; Abū Bakr agrees at the Hūd occurrence, and al-Bazzī agrees at the last Luqmān occurrence, yā bunayya aqimi al-ṣalāh.
NASHR:v2p289/r1.anchor: روى حفص بفتح الياء في الستة

NASHR:v2p289/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p289/r3.speaker: ابن كثير
NASHR:v2p289/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr lightens and gives sukūn to the yāʾ in the first Luqmān occurrence.
NASHR:v2p289/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير الأول من لقمان وهو (يا بني لا تشرك) بتخفيف الياء وإسكانها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p139/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p139/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p139/r2.claim: Luqman’s counsel warns against associating partners, commands kindness to parents and awareness of God, prayer, enjoining right, forbidding wrong and patience, and rejects pride while urging humility in walking and speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p139/r2.anchor: من التحذير من الإشراك ، ومن الأمر ببر الوالدين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p49/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p49/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p49/r6.claim: The Quran guides and legislates for a community through material that may precede need, admonish or praise particular people, or address everyone fit to hear it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p49/r6.anchor: كتاب جاء لهدي أمة والتشريع لها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p49/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p49/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p49/r7.claim: Quranic legislation and ethical instruction uses broad principles to make religion easy to understand, preserve it through transmission, and give scholars room to derive rulings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p49/r7.anchor: وقد يكون مخاطبا به جميع من يصلح لخطابه ، وهو في جميع ذلك قد جاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p49/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p49/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p49/r8.claim: The Quran’s concise form is deliberate; God could have revealed much more or extended the Prophet’s lifetime, and 5:3 declares the completion of divine favor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p49/r8.anchor: فكما لا يجوز حمل كلماته على خصوصيات جزئية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p49/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p49/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p49/r9.claim: One must neither narrow general wording that is meant broadly nor generalize wording intended specifically or make a restricted statement absolute, since this confuses or defeats the intended meaning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p49/r9.anchor: لا يجوز تعميم ما قصد منه الخصوص ولا إطلاق ما قصد منه التقييد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p49/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p49/r10.speaker: ابن سيرين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p49/r10.claim: Ibn Sirin says the Kharijites applied threat verses revealed about polytheists to Muslims, producing the innovation of declaring people unbelievers for sin.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p49/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p49/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p49/r12.claim: Revelation accompanying events also demonstrates the Quran’s miraculous ability to answer spontaneously and refutes the claim that it is merely ancient tales.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p49/r12.anchor: وثمة فائدة أخرى عظيمة لأسباب النزول وهي أن في نزول القرآن عند حدوث حوادث دلالة على إعجازه
